exposure: early-onset severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (<34 weeks gestation)
late-onset severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (>=34 weeks gestation)
cohort: The study cohort comprised 400 women admitted with early or late-onset severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia, diagnosed according to ACOG criteria.
finding: Maternal complications, including pulmonary edema, DIC, eclampsia, and mortality, were more severe and frequent in early-onset cases (20-34 weeks), highlighting increased risks.
mod_finding: Early-onset cases had higher cesarean rates, and timely delivery, especially via cesarean section, is emphasized for optimizing maternal and fetal outcomes.
gest_age: The study cohort was stratified based on gestational age at diagnosis of severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia: Group A (20-34 weeks) and Group B (>=34 weeks).
